narrative.overview: The guide is a set of engineering sheets. Each topic is one sheet with a title block (SHEET, SOURCE, TIME, STATUS), the home page is the cover sheet, and the lecturer's slides are pinned to the sheet like plotted prints. The world comes from the subject itself: DFDs and flowcharts are line drawings, so the frame speaks in drafting lines on cyanotype blue. The world owns the frame and leaves the reading column calm.
keyCharacteristics: Cyanotype ground with a faint 32px drafting grid outside the sheet.
Square corners everywhere; the only rounded shape is the DFD process box.
Drafting labels in tracked Chakra Petch; reading text in Sarabun at 18px.
One amber accent for exam-critical marks and the primary action.
A manual light/dark toggle: cyanotype (dark) and whiteprint (light) are the same world inverted.

rules.name: The One Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber marks what is examined or what to do next. It never decorates.

rules.name: The Meaning-Only Green Rule
rules.body: Green appears only to say "correct". A green page theme is rejected.

rules.name: The Calm Column Rule
rules.body: Drafting type stays in the frame (nav, title block, labels, headings). Paragraphs are always Sarabun.

rules.name: The Paper-On-Sheet Rule
rules.body: Only real paper (slides) casts a shadow. UI never does.

dos: Do keep every new page inside the drawing-set frame: sheet panel, title block, square corners, 1px lines.
Do use amber only for exam-critical marks and the next action.
Do use green for correct and red for wrong in any answer feedback, in both themes.
Do show the lecturer's real slide instead of redrawing it, with a caption naming lecture and page.
Do keep body text Sarabun 18px at about 70 characters and contrast at 4.5:1 or more in both themes.
Do give every motion a reduced-motion fallback that still shows the final state.
donts: Don't use a green or purple page theme; blue is the committed family.
Don't put the drafting grid behind reading text.
Don't add rounded cards, coloured side stripes, gradients or glow shadows.
Don't let a feature work by mouse only; every click interaction needs a keyboard path.
